HxResult HxMenuAddItem ( HxMenu_t *  pMenu,
HxMenuItem_t *  pItem,
int32_t  index 
)

Add a menu item to a menu.

HxMenuAddItem adds a menu item to a specific menu at desired index at runtime. Marker types may not be added to the root menu.

If the index is greater than the current number of items or if it is set to -1, the menu item is appended to the end of the menu.

Parameters:
pMenu IN: Pointer to a menu
pItem IN: Pointer to a menu item
index IN: Zero-based index for the menu item, or -1 to add to the end.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxMenuAddMarker ( HxMenu_t *  pMenu,
uint32_t  itemID,
const char *  display 
)

Add a scrollable item to a menu.

HxMenuAddMarker adds a menu item which appears within a potentially scrollable region of the menu. If enough markers are added to the same menu, the markers will scroll, instead of expand, hiding items that might not fit on the screen. The scrollable region of any menu always occurs at the bottom of the menu, below normal menu items. To listen to a specific menu marker action use the kHxMenuMarkerSelected or kHxMenuMarkerIDSelected message. See messagedomain.h for more information. Markers may not be added to the root menu.

Parameters:
pMenu IN: Pointer to a menu
fileId IN: associated id with the file, cannot be 0
display IN: string to be displayed on the menu
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxMenuDelete ( HxMenu_t *  pMenu  ) 

Delete a menu and all of its submenus.

HxMenuDelete decrements the refrence count of menu by 1. If the reference count is 0 it deletes a menu created from an earlier call to HxMenuNew. It is not necessary to call this function when quitting the application.

Parameters:
pMenu IN: Pointer to the menu to delete
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

Find an item by its id.

This function the menu item and its containing Menu container. This does not search markers in the menu, since the index value would be invalid for them.

HxResult HxMenuItemNew ( uint32_t  id,
const char *  pString,
HxMenuItemType  type,
int32_t  state,
HxImageDescription_t *  pIcon,
char  shortcut,
void *  pData,
HxMenuItem_t **  hItem 
)

Create a menu item.

HxMenuItemNew creates a new menu item. Its reference count is set to 1.

If the type is kHxMenuSubmenu, pData points to the HxMenu_t submenu, and the reference count of the submenu is incremented by 1. To listen to a specific menu item action use the kHxMenuItemIDSelected message. See messagedomain.h for more information.

The icon associated with the menu item should have an alpha channel to properly render with a transparent background. Color-keyed icons are not supported.

Parameters:
id IN: Unique ID for the menu item, defined by app, or kHxWidgetAutoID to auto-generate the ID
pString IN: String displayed by menu item
type IN: Type of the menu item
state IN: Initial state of the menu item
pIcon IN: Left icon associated with the item or NULL.
shortcut IN: Shortcut character or 0 for no shortcut.
pData IN: NULL or an optional submenu.
hItem OUT: Handle to the created menu item, set to NULL on failure
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails.

HxResult HxMenuItemSetIcon ( HxMenuItem_t *  pItem,
HxMenuItemIconPosition  position,
HxImageDescription_t *  pIcon 
)

Add or replace an Icon on the menu.

HxMenuItemSetIcon sets the right ot left icon for the menu item.

The icon associated with the menu item should have an alpha channel to properly render with a transparent background. Color-keyed icons are not supported.

A menu item can only have one icon; if you set a right icon, the left one is removed, and vice versa.

Parameters:
pItem IN: Pointer to a menu item
position IN: position of the icon: lefot or right
pIcon IN: image to use for the icon.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxMenuRegisterShortcut ( HxMenu_t *  pMenu,
uint32_t  id,
int32_t  shortcut 
)

Add a shortcut to a menu.

HxMenuRegisterShortcut adds a shortcut to a menu. It is not necessary to associate the shortcut character with a menu item, so this function allows applications to enable Menu+Key shortcuts that aren't shown in the menus.

You can also pass one of the values from the HxMenuSymbol type as a shortcut here to associate Menu + arrow key with a command.

Parameters:
pMenu IN: Pointer to a menu
id IN: ID sent with the message
shortcut IN: Character which will trigger the message
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxMenuShow ( HxMenu_t *  pMenu,
int32_t  x,
int32_t  y 
)

Show a menu.

HxMenuShow shows the menu at the specified coordinates. The x and y coordinates are ignored for root menus. A kHxMenuAboutToShow message will be sent to alert the application. If the menu is already showing, this call will do nothing; if you need to move the menu on the screen, you should hide it and then show it at a new location. Attempting to show an empty menu will result in an assertion in debug builds or return invalid area returned release builds.

If the popup menu would extend off the edge of the screen with the provided x and y coordinates, it will be automatically adjusted to fit onto the screen by moving it up or to the left.

Parameters:
pMenu IN: Pointer to menu
x IN: x coordinate of menu
y IN: y coordinate of menu
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.
